raw_case_text:
Patient information: a 35-year-old man presented with non-pruritic generalized scaly red patches in the last one month. Initially the lesions appeared on the face which then extended to other parts of the body, including the palms and soles. The patient also complained of hair loss since the appearance of the patches. Past and family history of similar lesions were absent. A history of painless genital ulcer was denied. The patient was diagnosed with HIV two months prior to admission and had been on antiretroviral therapy (ART). However, the ART was temporarily discontinued due to suspected drug allergy. The patient admitted to having the last sexual encounter three months prior to admission with his wife. He also reported sexual contact with prostitutes without protection.
Clinical findings: on physical examination, the patient was in a good general state with normal vital signs. Dermatological examinations showed generalized squamous annular erythematous plaques and erythematous macules (Figure 1). Diffuse nonscarring alopecia was observed on the scalp. Multiple ulcers and erythematous plaques were observed on the penis.
Timeline of current episode: history of disease is described as a timeline (Figure 2).
Diagnostic assessment: blood examination indicated anemia, hypoalbuminemia, and hypoglobulinemia. Syphilis serologic examination results showed positive VDRL with titer 1: 128 and TPHA.
Diagnosis: based on the results of anamnesis and physical examination, the patient was diagnosed with psoriasiform secondary syphilis.
Therapeutic interventions: the patient was given 2.4 million units of intramuscular benzathine G penicillin injection on the right and left gluteus. The ART was planned to be resumed.
Follow-up and outcome of interventions: the next day the patient experienced a high fever without the appearance of erythematous macules which subsided following paracetamol administration. On the seventh day, the skin lesions showed significant improvement (Figure 3). The erythematous plaques had thinned and decreased in number; ulcers on the penis looked shallower. A follow-up VDRL titer examination was planned in three months. In addition, the patient's wife was also recommended to do a syphilis and HIV screening examination.
Patient perspective: the patient felt so relieved that the extensive rash and alopecia could eventually be resolved. Aside from the painful Benzathine Penicillin injection, he did not have any complaints about the whole treatment regimen.
Informed consent: the patient had given consent for publication.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 35-year-old HIV-positive man presented with a 1-month history of a generalized non-pruritic scaly erythematous rash beginning on his face and spreading to his trunk, palms, and soles, accompanied by diffuse scalp hair loss.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: One month prior to admission, the patient noticed non-itchy scaly red patches on his face that progressively generalized across his trunk, extremities, palms, and soles, alongside diffuse scalp alopecia.
subjective.past_medical_history: Diagnosed with HIV infection 2 months prior to admission (antiretroviral therapy was temporarily held due to a suspected drug allergy); no personal or family history of psoriasis. Reported unprotected sexual intercourse with commercial sex workers as well as sexual contact with his wife 3 months prior to admission; denied noticing a prior painless genital chancre.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for generalized non-pruritic scaly plaques and scalp alopecia; denied prior painless genital ulcer awareness (though penile ulcers were found on exam). Temporarily discontinued ART.

objective.physical_examination: General condition and vital signs were normal. Dermatological examination revealed generalized psoriasiform/squamous annular erythematous plaques and macules involving the face, trunk, extremities, palms, and soles, diffuse non-scarring scalp alopecia, and multiple ulcers and erythematous plaques on the penis.
objective.routine_investigations: Blood tests demonstrated anemia, hypoalbuminemia, and hypoglobulinemia.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed psoriasiform secondary syphilis with syphilitic alopecia and penile ulcers in an HIV-positive patient, established via high-titer serum VDRL (1:128) and positive TPHA. Treated with a single intramuscular dose of benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units divided between the right and left gluteal muscles (complicated the next day by a self-limited febrile Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction managed with oral paracetamol), with significant thinning and regression of the psoriasiform plaques and penile ulcers by day 7 and plans to resume ART and screen his wife.
